subject: Request: SCCs segmentation + order form amendment for HealthBridge DPA

Cc: procurement@healthbridge.com, legal@healthbridge.com
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines and SCCs segregation proposal

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our contract review we circulated a proposed DPA redline internally and have two asks we wanted to put on the table before moving to procurement:  

1) SCCs module selection — HealthBridge (controller) wants the contract to reference controller-to-processor SCCs with an explicit carveout for cross-border analytics processing. We included suggested language to limit transfer scope and a reference to a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA).

2) Order form amendment — we need a short addendum to the Order Form that enumerates data locality regions and a subprocessor notice window (45 days). Minimal change but procurement asked that it be explicit.

Please see attached: HB-DPA-proposed-redlines.pdf with inline comments. Key ask: can Redwood accept the TIA approach and the 45-day subprocessor notice? If not, what alternative do you propose? We need alignment to scope internal approvals.

Proposed timeline: we hope to finalize redlines this week and hand to procurement for signature next week. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Anna Kovac
Legal — HealthBridge Solutions

--- Attachment: HB-DPA-proposed-redlines.pdf (PDF, 78KB) ---

Subject: Re: DPA redlines and SCCs segregation proposal

Anna — thanks for the clear note and the redline. Quick response while I pull legal in.

Summary of Redwood position (high level):
- SCCs / TIA: We are open to a Transfer Impact Addendum that captures the assessment for non-EEA subprocessors and any additional safeguards. Redwood prefers SCC-module language that maintains our right to route requests to alternative compatible model variants in other regions for availability (we'll include a code-of-conduct style clause to limit permanent data export).
- Subprocessor notice: 45 days is within our typical window; operationally we ask for a 30-day rolling notice for critical subprocessor changes, but can accept 45 days if HealthBridge requires it in contract.
- Controller/Processor roles: The proposed DPA currently reads ambiguous in two places (Sections 2.1 and 4.3). We need explicit controller responsibilities for data subject requests and a processor only obligation for telemetry used for model quality.

Next steps: I've looped in Karthik (legal lead) and Monica (security/compliance ops) to draft precise redline counters. Can you confirm whether HealthBridge expects the TIA to be executed as an exhibit to the MSA or as a standalone addendum to the DPA? That affects signing order.

If helpful we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the redline. Proposed times: Mon 11:00am or Mon 3:00pm PT.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed MSA amendment language + TIA template

Anna / team —

Thanks for the redline and the patience. Quick note with concrete edits attached: I prepared two files — redline-msacontrib.docx (MSA amendment language that ties Order Form locality fields to the DPA) and tia-template.docx (a short Transfer Impact Addendum template that captures subprocessors, technical and organizational measures, and a residual risk statement). Highlights below:  

- MSA amendment (attached) will add a new Section 12.5: "Order Form Data Locality and Subprocessor Notice". It references the Order Form field "dataRegions" and mandates a 45-day notice for non-critical subprocessor addition; critical changes require 30-day notice + acceptance.
- SCCs: We propose using the controller-to-processor modules (Module 1 + Module 2) with an explicit clause permitting transient cross-border analytics for inference latency reasons, subject to the TIA review.
- TIA approach: prefer executed as an exhibit to the MSA (Exhibit D) so it lives with the master contract and can be updated by mutual written agreement. This avoids signing multiple separate instruments later.
- Evidence: Monica, can you prepare the export-control mapping and the list of current subprocessors (jurisdictional table) to attach to the TIA within two business days? That will unblock HealthBridge legal review.

If HealthBridge prefers the TIA as a standalone addendum, we can accommodate but will flag that procurement must sign it concurrently with the DPA (DocuSign envelope).

I attached the raw docx files for markup. Please review and send back any line edits. If you're good, Rishi — happy for you to re-schedule the call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
